title: Open letter to new founders: no shortcuts, learn by doing, go deep in one niche
summary: John Rush's blunt letter says startup success has no shortcut. It takes years of reps, many skills learned by doing, and total focus. He then lays out what works: pick a narrow niche, become top 1%, educate the audience, build micro MVPs, and treat it as a marathon.

principles.text: No quick, risk-free path to startup success exists; anyone promising one is lying, and most makers fail repeatedly.
principles.quote: There is no easy, quick, risk-free & proven way to succeed.

principles.text: "Overnight" success hides years of reps; his fast results come from 20 years of building startups.
principles.quote: I may start a product today and reach $30k MRR in 6 months. Can I teach you this? NO! I can do that because I've spent 20 years building startups.

principles.text: Founders must be above average across many skills, and the only way to learn them is by doing, not consuming.
principles.quote: No amount of reading, watching youtube, consuming the courses and bookmarking the tweets will help, if you don't actually apply this knowledge right away.

principles.text: Don't mix fun and education; consuming content trains you to get dopamine from consuming instead of acting.
principles.quote: Don't mix fun & education. It inevitably kills your bias for action. Suddenly you get dopamine when u consume, not when u act.

principles.text: Pick a narrow niche you understand deeply instead of targeting a wide audience.
principles.quote: Don't spread to wide audiences. Pick a narrow niche. You should have some connection to the audience or be able to understand the audience and emulate their thought, pain, taste, and desires.

principles.text: Iterate for months with micro MVPs and manual work for your audience; the tool that gains attention shows where to invest.
principles.quote: Spend months iterating with micro MVPs and doing things manually for your audience and inevitably, one of the tools/services will gain more attention, and you'll clearly see you need to put more time into it.
